fatal_errors: The proposed irradiation resistance and grain-size stability under irradiation are not supported by the cited evidence.

Evidence E4 directly reports that grain refinement had negligible effects on passivation and pitting in the tested CoCrFeMnNi alloys, yet it was presented as supporting evidence and no conflicting evidence was acknowledged.
explanation: This is a testable alternative hypothesis about ultrafine-grained stainless steel, not a reconstruction of the target AlCoCrFeNi coating study. It replaces atmospheric plasma spraying and 550 °C annealing with severe plastic deformation and replaces sulfuric-acid and 900 °C molten-salt exposures with chloride, reactor-water, and irradiation environments. It nevertheless shares limited mechanistic content with the target: grain refinement, chromium enrichment of passive films, and reduced corrosion current. The same-alloy coarse-grained control, electrochemistry, XPS/TEM/EBSD, pit measurements, and explicit falsification criterion make the experiment reasonably discriminating, although SPD may introduce residual stress, texture, and defect-density confounders that should be separately controlled. Evidence E2 supports Cr-enriched passivation in many UFG stainless steels, but E3–E4 caution that sluggish diffusion and high-entropy behavior can suppress the grain-size effect in HEAs. No cited result substantiates the claims concerning thermal cycling or irradiation. Boundaries are qualitatively stated but lack alloy composition, temperature, dose, water chemistry, and exposure-time limits.
